title: Pride and Humility
aka: pride is the beginning of sin
lead: Across the Bible pride is the creature forgetting the Creator, and God brings the proud low and lifts the humble. Proverbs warns that pride goes before a fall; the prophets mock proud kings who would be gods; Jesus says the one who brings himself low will be raised up; and Christian tradition, through the Latin of Sirach 10, came to call pride the beginning of all sin.

sections.h: Pride and humility across the Bible
sections.b:
Proverbs says it in a line: "Pride comes before a crash, / a lofty spirit before a stumble" (Proverbs 16:18), and "Pride brings a person down low, / and the one who is low in spirit takes hold of honor" (Proverbs 29:23). The prophets turn the warning on kings who make themselves gods. The king of Babylon said, "I will make myself the Most High's equal" (Isaiah 14:14); the ruler of Tyre said, "I am a god!" (Ezekiel 28:2). Nebuchadnezzar learned that "Those who walk in pride he is able to humble" (Daniel 4:37).

The New Testament keeps the same reversal. Mary sings that God "has pulled rulers down from thrones / and raised the lowly high" (Luke 1:52). Jesus says, "Everyone who raises himself up will be brought low, and the one who brings himself low will be raised up" (Luke 18:14). James and Peter quote Proverbs: "God takes his stand against the proud, but to the humble he gives grace" (James 4:6; 1 Peter 5:5). Paul asks believers, "with a lowly mind, rank others above yourselves" (Philippians 2:3), after the example of Christ who humbled himself (Philippians 2:5-8).
